instructions: The night before, or at least 1 hour ahead: cut the lamb into 3/4-inch cubes and leave the fat on. Slice the onion thinly and the garlic thinly. In a bowl, toss the lamb with the onion, the garlic, the cornstarch and 2 tbsp of the oil. Cover and refrigerate.
When you're ready to cook, take the lamb out of the fridge. If you're using bamboo skewers, put 8 of them in water to soak for 30 minutes. Metal skewers need nothing.

Put 1 1/2 cups of rice, 3 cups of water and 1/4 tsp of the salt in a medium pot. Bring it to a boil over high heat, then turn it to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on.
Heat the oven broiler to high, with a rack 4 inches from the heat. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a wire rack on it.

Toast the cumin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 1 minute, until they smell toasty. Add 1 tsp of the pepper flakes and stir for 10 seconds. Transfer both to a mortar or a spice grinder and crush them coarsely, so you can still see pieces. Put this spice mix in a small bowl.
Put the remaining 1 tbsp pepper flakes in a second small bowl for the table.
Shake the onion and garlic off the lamb and throw them away. Thread the lamb onto the 8 skewers, pressing the cubes together. Sprinkle 1 tsp of the salt over all sides.
Lay the skewers on the rack. Broil for 4 minutes, then turn them over and broil for 3 minutes, until the edges are browned and crisp.
Dust the skewers with half the spice mix. Broil for 1 minute more. Turn them, dust with the rest of the spice mix and broil for 1 minute.
You're cooking the lamb to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one cube there. No thermometer? Cut one cube open. It's done when it's just barely pink and the juices run clear.
Meanwhile, slice the cucumber into rounds.
Taste a piece. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice and the cucumber, with the bowl of pepper flakes at the table for anyone who wants more heat.
advance_prep_notes: marinate the lamb at least 1 hour ahead, or overnight
method_notes: Lead is Not Quite Nigella (5.0 from 15 ratings, under the 20 needed; the other same-dish versions had 7 to 8 ratings or none, so none could lead properly). All the versions agree on fatty lamb shoulder in small cubes, coarsely crushed cumin seeds and chili flakes, and a second dusting of spice partway through cooking. They differ on the marinade: Not Quite Nigella and The Woks of Life keep it to oil, with onion, garlic and a little starch, while Andy Cooks uses soy sauce and sesame. This one follows Not Quite Nigella, with no soy or sesame, so it stays gluten-free. It is cooked under the broiler instead of on charcoal, and most of the chili flakes go on the side to keep the skewers mild. Sources serve with bread; rice and cucumber keep it gluten-free.
